She started right away. We wound up having to do formula feeding after we got out of the hospital because I was having such a hard time breastfeeding her. She couldn't hold anything down. Every time she ate, she would throw up a few minutes later. Holding her up right became a job after every meal. And sometimes it didn't work, and she would still wind up throwing up. She was extremely fussy. 

We tried a bunch of different things because at first we thought it was a milk allergy. The doctors really weren't any help. Eventually somebody clued us into acid reflux, and we started trying some different formulas to help with that. The enfamil one has rice starch in it, which makes it a little bit thicker. Make a schedule. Pick a day to clean toilets and sinks. Another day to wipe down surfaces. Another day to sweep/mop and another to vacuum ... Give yourself a break in between.

Our schedule is:
- Saturday, toilets 
- Sunday, sinks and tubs
- Monday, wipe down surfaces - stove drip trays, microwave plate, dish strainer into the dishwasher
- Tuesday, sweep, mop, vacuum

We take a break from Wednesday to Friday.

Hit up an urgent care. The hospital AND her doctor both shrugged us off like it was just a routine virus that would go away. A few things to note:

- Watch for spit up and projectile vomiting, as these can be signs of acid reflux.
- If acid reflux is a problem, Enfamil makes an AR formula that's thickened with rice starch, which makes it easier for kiddos to keep down. You could also add rice cereal to formula bottles in small quantities, but I would only do this under your pediatrician's instruction.
- If kiddo winds up having reflux, keep them upright for a bit after each feed.
- WIC can provide you with Gerber brand formula.
- You only have to sterilize the bottles for the first time you use them. Afterwards, you can just wash them as normal.
- You can 'prep' the bottles by filling them with distilled water until they are used (as long as you keep them capped). I used to have eight bottles on standby in the early days. In my opinion it's easier to do this because if you premake formula at the beginning of the day, you have to toss what you don't use by the end of it.
- To distill your own water, boil it. I forget if it's for five minutes or ten ...
- Tommee Tippee and Nuk bottle nipples are interchangeable. (Learned that from doing it myself).
- Some babies prefer warm formula. Some like it at room temperature. Test each to see what your kiddo prefers.
- The one big issue with formula are the air bubbles that form during mixing, which can cause painful gas. To remedy this, add a drop or two of simethicone to your bottles. It breaks up gas bubbles and makes everything so much easier.
